newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Minister says Russia must go for economic growth.
newsitem.headline: Minister says Russia must go for economic growth.

text.p: Economy Minister Yevgeny Yasin called in a letter published on Tuesday for urgent efforts to boost Russian industrial output and forge conditions for growth.

The letter, addressed to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and published in the Nezavisimaya Gazeta daily newspaper, said neither the 1997 budget nor the government's medium-term growth forecasts were realistic.

"If the existing trends in the economy are continued without energetic and purposeful efforts to break them and create real conditions for economic growth, the situation will in all probability continue to get worse," said Yasin.
He said lower Russian interest rates -- a key government aim -- would not on their own be enough to stimulate growth quickly.
"We cannot count on this," he said. "It could take too long, during which time the degradation of the economy will continue, possibly with irreversible consequences."
Russian officials have repeatedly said the economy was about to grow and a three-year plan released last week predicted five percent annual growth in gross domestic product by 2000.
But there are few signs of a lasting turnaround and Yasin said old policies of "concessions and indulgencies" to lobby groups was dragging Russia into an abyss.
"The 1997 budget reflects this former policy. It does not envisage any future except continuing the trends which have already been formed," he said.
He said the three-year plan did not examine properly the real risks facing the Russian economy.
Yasin listed tax and military reform as two priority government tasks and said both spending and revenue forecasts should be cut, even if this meant cutting social spending.
